exercise.instruction: Write the program: a class Animal with a public virtual void speak() { } (empty body), then a class Dog : public Animal whose void speak() override prints "Woof". In main create Dog d and call d.speak().
hints: Hint 1: class Animal { public: virtual void speak() { } };
Hint 2: class Dog : public Animal { public: void speak() override { std::cout << "Woof" << std::endl; } };
Hint 3: In main: Dog d; d.speak();

quiz.question: What does class Dog : public Animal mean?
options: Dog is the base class of Animal
Dog is an instance of Animal

quiz.question: What does override do?
options: Checks the derived method truly overrides a virtual base method

quiz.question: Why use a virtual destructor in a base class?
options: So derived destructors run when deleting through a base pointer
